title: Who can start a skill?
intro: Two optional frontmatter fields change who is allowed to invoke a skill. Pick a setting for a skill named deploy and see what changes.

show.title: You and Claude can both start it
show.detail: By default you can type /deploy, and Claude can load the skill when your request matches its description. The description sits in context; the full skill loads when it is invoked.

trace.text: May also load the skill by itself when a request matches the description.

show.title: Only you can start it
show.detail: Claude cannot invoke the skill on its own, and its description is not kept in context. This suits actions with side effects, where you want to choose the moment yourself.

trace.text: Cannot start the deploy skill on its own; it can suggest that you run /deploy.

show.title: Only Claude can start it
show.detail: You cannot invoke the skill as a command, but Claude can still load it when relevant. This suits background knowledge that is not an action in itself.

trace.text: Loads the skill when the conversation calls for it.

fallback.title: Pick a setting
fallback.detail: This demo scripts the three cases above. Choose one to see who can invoke the skill.

quiz.question: You want a skill that only runs when you type its command. Which frontmatter field do you add?
quiz.explanation: disable-model-invocation: true stops Claude from invoking the skill on its own, while you can still run it with its slash command.
